rows.text: Which parameters are plotted in the Ellingham diagram?

Which of the following compounds will NOT undergo the Finkelstein reaction with NaI via \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) pathway?

**I**: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2Br}\), (bromomethyl)benzene

**II**: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5Br}\), bromobenzene

**III**: \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH{=}CHBr}\), (E)-(2-bromoethenyl)benzene

**IV**: \(\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CH_2Br}\), (bromomethyl)cyclohexane

figure.note: Four skeletal structures labelled I-IV: I benzene ring with a CH2-Br chain; II benzene ring with Br directly on the ring; III benzene ring with a CH=CH-Br chain drawn trans (E); IV cyclohexane ring with a CH2-Br chain.

rows._flag: Structures I-IV are drawn; typed in the stem from the drawing (III's double bond is drawn trans).

rows.text:
Which one amongst the following is the most efficient way of synthesizing n-propyl benzene?

**(I)** \(\mathrm{C_6H_6} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ KOH,\ NH_2\text{-}NH_2,\ \Delta}]{\mathrm{(i)\ CH_3CH_2COCl,\ anhydrous\ AlCl_3}}\)

**(II)** \(\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3CH_2CH_2Cl} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{anhydrous\ AlCl_3}}\)

**(III)** \(\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3CH_2CH_2OH} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+}}\)

**(IV)** \(\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+}}\)

figure.note: Four routes labelled (I)-(IV), each starting from a benzene ring: (I) arrow with '(i) H3C-CH2-C(=O)-Cl (skeletal), anhydrous AlCl3' above and '(ii) KOH, NH2-NH2, Δ' below; (II) + H3C-CH2-CH2-Cl, arrow with 'anhydrous AlCl3'; (III) + H3C-CH2-CH2-OH, arrow with 'H+'; (IV) + H3C-CH=CH2, arrow with 'H+'. No products are drawn.

rows._flag: Reaction schemes are drawn with skeletal reagents; typed in the stem as condensed formulae.

rows.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
rows.text:
Which amongst the following are chiral compounds?

**(I)** 4,4-dimethylcyclohexan-1-amine

**(II)** but-3-en-2-amine, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)CH{=}CH_2}\)

**(III)** 4-ethenyl-4-methylcyclohexan-1-one

**(IV)** 2-methylcyclohex-2-en-1-ol

(Wedge and hash bonds as drawn in the figure.)

figure.note: Four structures labelled (I)-(IV): (I) cyclohexane with H2N (hashed) and H (wedged) on C1 and two CH3 groups (one wedged, one hashed) on C4; (II) Me-CH(NH2)-CH=CH2 with H hashed and NH2 wedged on the stereocentre; (III) cyclohexanone with Me (wedged) and a vinyl group (hashed) on C4; (IV) cyclohexene ring with OH (wedged) and H (hashed) on C1 and CH3 on the adjacent ring double-bond carbon C2.

rows._flag: Structures are drawn with stereo bonds; typed in the stem as constitutional IUPAC names only (the stereo bonds stay in the figure).

figure.note: Four structures labelled (I)-(IV): (I) cyclopropene ring with a CH3 on each of the three carbons and a positive charge (circled +); (II) six-membered ring with O at the bottom, two C=C double bonds and a positive charge on the carbon opposite O; (III) seven-membered ring with three C=C double bonds and a negative charge (circled -) on the remaining carbon; (IV) square four-membered ring with two double bonds (cyclobutadiene).

rows.subtopic: Properties of Matter and Their Measurement
rows.text: Why is it harder to compress liquids and solids relative to gases?
options: Molecules are closer to each other in solids and liquids.
Due to the presence of electron-nuclear attraction in solids and liquids.
Due to the absence of electron-nuclear attraction in solids and liquids.
Solids and liquids have definite volume.

rows.text: Related to the Freundlich adsorption isotherm, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: It holds good over a wide range of pressures.
The value of \(\frac{1}{n}\) is between 0 and 1.
The Freundlich adsorption isotherm equation is an empirical equation.
It is used for the adsorption of both gases and solutions.

rows.subtopic: Enthalpies for Different Types of Reactions
rows.text:
Consider the following reaction:

\(\mathrm{CH_4(g) \longrightarrow C(g) + 4H(g)}\); \(\Delta_a H^0 = 1665\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\)

Which of the statements is FALSE?
options: \(\Delta_a H^0\) is the mean bond enthalpy of a C-H bond.
All four C-H bonds in \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) are identical in bond length and energy.
The energy required to break individual C-H bonds in successive steps is different.
Mean C-H bond enthalpies differ slightly from compound to compound.

rows.text: In two solutions X (hexane and benzene) and Y (water and HCl), what types of deviations from Raoult's law are observed?
options: No deviation (ideal behaviour) and negative deviation, respectively.
Negative deviation and positive deviation, respectively.
Positive deviation and negative deviation, respectively.
Positive deviation and no deviation (ideal behaviour), respectively.
